page: Amazon Web Services g6e.xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server instance running on the Nitro hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with a base clock speed of 3.4 GHz, offering 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, which provides a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For hardware acceleration, it includes a single NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPU equipped with 45 GB of VRAM. Local storage is provided via a 250 GB NVMe SSD, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reveal a specialized capability profile. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%, while multi-core CPU performance is average. Conversely, memory bandwidth benchmarks for both read and write operations are weak, falling into the bottom 25%. Despite these memory throughput limitations, the server delivers top-tier performance in large language model inference. Benchmarks for both small (135M) and medium (7B) models place the instance in the top 10% for both prompt processing and text generation speeds.

The primary tradeoff of the g6e.xlarge is its high-performance GPU capabilities contrasted against its modest 2 Gbps network baseline and weaker memory bandwidth. This makes the instance highly cost-efficient for localized GPU-bound tasks that do not require high-throughput network transfers or intensive database operations, as reflected in its weak performance in Redis and static web serving benchmarks. It is highly suited for machine learning inference, small to medium LLM execution, and graphics-intensive rendering workloads.

The hardware configuration is highlighted by a single NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPU with 45 GB of VRAM. While benchmark results indicate weaker memory bandwidth and average multi-core CPU performance, the instance delivers top-tier results in LLM inference, placing in the top 10% for prompt processing and text generation on 135M and 7B models. With a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, this instance represents a specialized hardware profile optimized for localized AI inference, rendering, and GPU-driven compute tasks rather than high-throughput database operations or general web serving.
